title: Tale of the Three Men and Our Lord Isa (मराठी)

keywords: tale of the three men and our lord isa
full_text:
Three travelers walking along an ancient desert trail discovered a heavy earthenware jar buried in the sand, overflowing with sparkling gold coins left behind by a forgotten caravan.

Overjoyed, they agreed to divide the gold equally among themselves. But having traveled all day in the heat, they were starving.

They sent the youngest traveler to the neighboring village to purchase bread, meat, and sweet cordials, while the two elder travelers guarded the treasure.

As the youth walked to the village, greed entered his soul: 'Why should I share this gold with two old men? If I put poison in their bread, all the treasure will be mine alone!' He purchased food, and mixed a potent, tasteless poison into the meat.

Meanwhile, sitting beside the gold jar, the two elder companions whispered together: 'Why should we divide the gold three ways? When the youth returns, let us strike him down with our staves, and divide the gold between the two of us!'

When the young traveler returned carrying the food, the two elders sprang upon him, struck him down, and buried his body in the sand.

They then sat down upon the treasure, laughed at their cleverness, and devoured the roasted meat and bread with greedy relish.

Within an hour, the poison took effect! The two elder companions collapsed upon the heap of gold, writhing in agony, perishing beside the treasure they had murdered to possess.

A venerable sage passing by saw the three lifeless bodies lying around the jar of gold, and said: 'Behold the bitter harvest of greed! The gold remains upon the sand, untouched and worthless, while the souls of those who coveted it have perished in their own snares.'
moral: Greed turns companions into murderers; he who schemes to hoard gold for himself brings his own ruin. [MR]
